overview: Atelectasis refers to the partial or complete collapse of a lung segment, lobe, or entire lung. It occurs when microscopic alveoli deflate or become fluid-filled, reducing the surface area available for gas exchange.
radiographic_findings: Direct sign: displacement of pulmonary interlobar fissures toward the collapsed region
Direct sign: increased radiopacity (density) in the affected collapsed lobe or segment
Indirect sign: ipsilateral elevation of the hemidiaphragm
Indirect sign: mediastinal and tracheal shift toward the side of collapse
Platelike or discoid linear subsegmental opacities (Fleischner lines)
common_symptoms: Subacute dyspnea or shallow breathing (often asymptomatic if subsegmental)
Decreased tactile fremitus and localized diminished breath sounds
Mild cough or clearing of the throat
Low-grade fever (frequently observed in postoperative surgical recovery settings)
causes_and_risk_factors: Obstructive: Mucus plugging, foreign body aspiration, endobronchial tumor
Compressive: Surrounding space-occupying lesion, pleural effusion, pneumothorax
Surfactant deficiency: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Hypoventilation: Recent general anesthesia, thoracic/abdominal surgical incisions, rib fractures causing splinting
diagnostic_information: Standard Chest Radiography (AP or PA view with inspiratory effort assessment)
High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the chest if obstruction is suspected
Fiberoptic bronchoscopy to directly visualize and clear endobronchial mucus plugs or tumors
treatment_approaches: Incentive spirometry and deep breathing exercises every 1-2 hours
Chest physiotherapy, postural drainage, and early postoperative ambulation
Positive Expiratory Pressure (PEP) therapy or continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP)
Bronchoscopic suctioning for refractory mucus impaction
Adequate analgesia to minimize respiratory splinting
when_to_seek_care: Development of high fever or productive purulent cough indicating secondary pneumonia

reliable_sources.title: Perioperative Pulmonary Care and Atelectasis Prevention
